title: Embroiderers tell the conquest story at Bayeux
summary: The Bayeux embroidery narrates the Norman conquest through wool stitched onto linen, combining a continuous story with borders of animals and other scenes.

claims.text: The Bayeux embroidery narrates the Norman conquest through wool stitched onto linen, combining a continuous story with borders of animals and other scenes.
The museum places creation after the 1066 conquest within the eleventh century. 1067–1100 is a conservative envelope; 1077 is not asserted as completion.
The makers are unknown. A commission by Bishop Odo for Bayeux Cathedral is a leading hypothesis, not an established identification of patron or workshop.

review.corroboration: Two Bayeux Museum explanations were compared for technique and chronology. They are one source family; uncertainties over the commission remain explicit.
